caption: A charger already plugged into the wall is connected to a laptop, and the small light on the connector comes on.

sa.check: A charger cable with a connector at its free end.
The connector is pushed into the laptop.
The small light on the connector comes on.
The charger's other end is already plugged into the wall.
The order is connect, then light.

pc.expect: The connector light is dark while the connector is loose and comes on when it seats in the laptop's port, and only then.
pc.fail: The connector is seated and its light stays dark; or the light is lit while the connector is still away from the laptop; or the laptop's own charging light comes on while the connector's light stays dark.

pc.expect: Once seated the light stays on while the connector stays in the port.
pc.fail: The light goes out again with the connector still seated; or switches between lit and dark while the connector is untouched; or the connector backs out of the port by itself.

pc.expect: The screen's battery indicator changes to charging when the connector seats and not before.
pc.fail: The screen shows a charging symbol before the connector reaches the port; or the screen goes dark as the connector seats; or the screen's picture changes to a different one at the moment of connecting.
pc.precondition: The laptop's screen is on and facing the viewer.

pc.expect: The cable hangs slack from the connector in a curve and stays attached to it.
pc.fail: The cable stands rigid in the air; or stretches like elastic as the connector is moved; or floats above the desk.

pc.expect: One laptop and one connector on one cable; the connector enters the port rather than the laptop's body; fingers stay outside the laptop.
pc.fail: The connector passes into the laptop's side away from the port; or a second connector or cable appears; or the connector vanishes; or the laptop changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The laptop's colour, the cable's colour and the desk stay the same apart from the light.
pc.fail: The laptop changes colour; or the cable changes colour or thickness; or the port moves along the laptop's side.
